page: Microsoft Azure F48amds_v7 is an x86_64 instance powered by a 48-core AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at 4.5 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 48 dedicated vCPUs with a 1:1 thread-to-core mapping, eliminating hyper-threading contention. The hardware features 384.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation, coupled with 5670 GB of bundled high-speed local NVMe SSD storage. There are no onboard graphics processing units. Instruction set support includes AVX-512 extensions such as AVX-512 VNNI and BF16, alongside cryptographic acceleration flags including AES and SHA_NI.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier execution across compute and memory workloads. The instance achieved top-decile scores in stress-ng single-core (3765.29) and multi-core (175742.28) evaluations, as well as PassMark CPU operations (98150.08). Memory throughput is robust, showing 9285.95 GB/sec in cached 16 KB read tests and 177.17 GB/sec in large-block uncached writes. Data processing metrics reflect high sustained throughput, with 130.02 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and top-tier PassMark database operation scores (38963.07). CPU-based small and medium LLM inference shows competitive performance, though large parameter models drop to mid-range token throughput due to the absence of dedicated accelerators.

From a cost-efficiency and deployment standpoint, the F48amds_v7 delivers balanced high-density resources by pairing full physical core dedication with an expanded memory footprint and extensive local NVMe capacity. Because storage is bundled locally, it provides strong input/output efficiency without requiring detached block storage for scratch workloads, though public IPv4 addresses are not included complimentary. It is suited for in-memory databases, large-scale Redis caching clusters, high-throughput database workloads, and compute-heavy analytics pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure F48amds_v7 is a compute and memory-focused instance powered by a 48-core AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz with dedicated physical core allocation. It features 384.0 GB of RAM (8.0 GB per vCPU) and includes 5670 GB of local NVMe SSD storage without integrated GPUs. Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the top decile for both single-thread and multi-thread compute tasks, supported by AVX-512 and BF16 instruction sets. Memory performance is equally strong, delivering high write throughput and recording 130.02 million Redis operations per second alongside top-tier database benchmark results. The generous memory-to-core ratio and rapid bundled local disk deliver effective density for resource-intensive applications. It is well matched for high-throughput database operations, in-memory caching platforms, large-scale compression, and data-intensive analytical pipelines.
